body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

يقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب الراءات عقد هذا الباب لصفة عارضة وهي الترقيق الذي تتصف به الراء، فقد سبق أن التغليظ صفة لكل الحروف المستعلية وأن الترقيق صفة لكل الحروف المستفلة وأن التغليظ يعرض في ثلاثة من الحروف المستفلة وهي الراء واللام والألف، فهذه الحروف الثلاثة مستفلة ومع ذلك يعرض فيها التغليظ، وهذا التغليظ لما كان صفة عارضة لم نذكره، والمؤلف رحمه الله تعالى ذكر ما يتعلق بالراءت ثم ذكر ما يتعلق باللامات والألفات التي معها فبدأ بالراءات فقال:
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The author (may God have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the rāʾs." He set up this chapter for an accidental quality, namely the thinning of the sound that characterises the rāʾ. It has already been established that thickening is a quality of all the elevated letters and that thinning is a quality of all the lowered letters, and that thickening occurs accidentally in three of the lowered letters, namely the rāʾ, the lām and the alif. These three letters are lowered, and yet thickening occurs in them accidentally. Since this thickening was an accidental quality, we did not mention it [earlier]. The author (may God, be He exalted, have mercy on him) mentioned what pertains to the rāʾs, then mentioned what pertains to the lāms and the alifs that go with them; and he began with the rāʾs, saying:

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
The Arabic stops at 'saying:', immediately before the lines of verse that were to be quoted. The verse is not in the source and nothing has been supplied for it.

'Elevated' (mustaʿliyah) and 'lowered' (mustafilah) are the standard categories of Arabic phonetics used in this discipline, describing the raising or lowering of the back of the tongue; 'thickening' (tafkhīm) and 'thinning' (tarqīq) are the resulting qualities of the sound.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
